transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Maria Gomez, Jordan Lee, Samir Nair, Leah Brooks, Priya Anand

Auto-generated summary: some billing adjustments on dedicated capacity, K M S rotation ask from security, runbook updates and next steps captured.

[00:00] Alex Chen (AE): okay uh good afternoon everyone thanks for jumping on, want to keep this tight 45 minutes, lots to cover, Samir i think you led the ticket on the billing side, do you want to kick us off?

[00:18] Samir Nair (Finance): yeah thanks Alex, so, we noticed two spikes in Jan month to date, one relates to a mis-scheduling of reserved capacity where burst policies kicked in and also a smaller set of jobs that were hitting dedicated pools overnight so cost shifted, i have a preliminary csv i pasted into the ticket but want to talk through what telemetry we can add so we dont hit late surprises.

[00:40] Leah Brooks (Security): yeah and, just to flag, one of the surges coincided with a KMS rotate attempt in staging. It looks like the rotation script retried and temporarily ramped requests to the KMS endpoint. Might be a script loop.

[01:05] Maria Gomez (SE): hmm ok, so probably a retry backoff missing, uh did the rotation run across all pods or a subset? Jordan do you have context?

[01:20] Jordan Lee (DevOps): yeah so from the k8s side it targeted the staging namespace, it was a cronjob that was supposed to update the secret and bounce pods, but due to a mis-labeled annotation the job requeued itself, so you got repeated KMS API calls. The annotation mismatch was between the new controller vs older one, so they interpreted it differently.

[01:45] Speaker 1 (Priya?): okay, can we, uh, separate staging keys from prod and have a rate-limiter on the controller so it wont hammer KMS?

[02:03] Jordan Lee: absolutely, we can add client-side throttling and backoff; we also should shift rotation to a leader-elect pattern so only one instance does the rotate.

[02:20] Alex Chen: and on the billing side Samir, is the cost due to KMS API charges material? i thought KMS costs are pretty small, more of the dedicated gpu hours are the heavy line items.

[02:36] Samir Nair: correct, KMS was small dollars but amplified by the dedicated hours which are tens of thousands when pooled. The extra burst capacity that fired off during the retries bumped us into a higher commit tier for a day, so the delta was non-trivial. We need better caps and a reconciliation workflow so we can attribute spikes to root cause quickly.

[03:05] Leah Brooks: From security perspective we need emergency rotation steps documented: if a key is accidentally rotated or compromised, who calls the change control, what tags to set, how to revoke. Right now the runbook is sparse.

[03:22] Maria Gomez: i can take a pass at the runbook, but need the exact people and their oncall rotations. Priya can you dump the oncall schedule?

[03:35] Priya Anand: yes i will send the schedule now, and i'll also add a column for SRE owners for the clusters.

[03:45] [small crosstalk]

[04:00] Alex Chen: great, also Maria, you mentioned a POC for automated rotation tooling that includes safety nets? can you outline what you would demo and ideal success criteria?

[04:18] Maria Gomez: sure, the POC would run in staging, it would: 1) perform a rotate using a canary pod, 2) validate secrets served to a test consumer, 3) if validation fails, trigger immediate rollback and raise an alert. Success criteria are: zero failed validations in canary, rollback completes within 2 minutes, and no more than one failed API call per rotation attempt. I'll put up a README.

[04:45] Jordan Lee: and we can simulate load, like multiple pods reading secrets simultaneously so we can watch KMS call volume. Also we should instrument to separate staging KMS endpoint calls in billing telemetry.

[05:05] Samir Nair: for reconciliation, i'll need a spreadsheet that maps sku / dedicated-pool-id to team owner and commit tier for the month. if we have that i can attribute costs to teams for chargebacks.

[05:22] Alex Chen: actionable. Let's define the short-term mitigations: 1) add client side throttle to rotation jobs, 2) temporary alert on KMS API rate increase, 3) reconcile last 30 days of dedicated pool consumption and send to finance.

[05:40] Leah Brooks: agree. Also recommend we add RBAC check for any account that can initiate rotation; make sure only service accounts with least privilege can call rotate.

[06:00] Alex Chen: do we need to open a support ticket with cloud provider? if there's a sudden quota behavior we might need to request a soft limit increase or at least clarify what's billable.

[06:15] Jordan Lee: probably not necessary yet, we should first fix the script. If we reproduce the surge then escalate.

[06:28] Speaker 2 (Samir): one more thing, the billing UI aggregations are a bit delayed, i will attach raw export to the ticket so Maria and Jordan can map events to timestamps.

[06:45] Maria Gomez: perfect, i also want to note that some of our older controllers still call the K V cache in a way that triggers rehydration, the transcript maybe surfaced as KV cache vs key value cache but it's a thing; that rehydration process adds latency and more KMS reads because we re-fetch secrets on pod start.

[07:10] Priya Anand: ok that explains multiple spikes overnight when infra runs scale tests.

[07:25] Alex Chen: ok, let's walk through owners and dates quickly so we have alignment. Samir you'll submit the csv by next Friday the 29th, Maria to deliver POC repo by 28th, Jordan to enable alert by 23rd, Leah to update runbook by 27th, Priya to circulate oncall schedule today. Any objections?

[07:48] Leah Brooks: none from security.

[08:00] Jordan Lee: no objections.

[08:10] Samir Nair: all good.

[08:22] Alex Chen: cool, last thing — do we want to schedule a 30 minute follow-up next Thursday to review POC and the billing file?

[08:30] Maria Gomez: yes please, i'm open.

[08:33] Priya Anand: i'll set a calendar hold.

[08:37] Alex Chen: great thanks everyone, i'll also drop links in the ticket: billing raw export, Maria's POC README once ready, and Leah's runbook draft. Meeting adjourned.

[08:50] End of recording.
